chunks: God has not begotten a son, nor is there any god besides Him. Had this been so, each god would have taken away what he had created with him, and some would have risen over the others. God is much too glorious for what they attribute (to Him)!
ai.seo_question: What is the logical proof for God's unity against polytheism?
ai.summary: In Shia tafsir, this verse is often cited to refute the concept of divine plurality by highlighting the logical necessity of a single, undivided Sovereign to maintain cosmic order. The phrase 'each god would take what he created' underscores that polytheism implies competition and potential chaos among deities, whereas the observed harmony of the universe testifies to Allah's absolute uniqueness (Tawhid al-Zat). This reasoning reinforces the belief that Allah is free from any partner or offspring, as described in Surah Al-Ikhlas.
